reason: The arm needs the circulation already connected to the lungs to receive oxygen and nutrients.
expectation: The arm will connect to the circulation and receive its blood supply.

effect: The arm is now connected to the heart and lungs, and fluid remains in its tissue spaces. The remaining goal is to return excess fluid to the blood.
reaction: The tissue inset makes the connection between blood supply and fluid buildup clear.
reason: The blind-ended lymphatic capillaries sit among tissue cells, so they appear suited to collecting fluid from the tissue spaces.
expectation: The capillaries will collect excess tissue fluid.

effect: The tissue spaces now have lymphatic capillaries that take in fluid and proteins. The collecting vessels appear to be the next part of the return route.
reaction: The flap-like openings make the collection step easier to picture.
reason: The collecting lymphatic vessels should carry fluid away from the capillaries.
expectation: The collecting vessels will connect to the capillaries and carry lymph onward.

effect: The collecting vessels now carry lymph onward, with muscle movement and valves helping it flow forward. The return ducts appear to be the next connection.
reaction: The paired muscle poses clarify how movement helps lymph flow.
reason: The lymphatic return ducts join large veins, so they should complete the route back toward the blood.
expectation: The ducts will connect the lymphatic vessels to the veins.

effect: The lymph pathways had to be connected to the supplied arm before the return ducts. The automatic combination made that connection.
reaction: The required order surprised me, but the compatibility feedback made the next step clear.
reason: The return ducts can now connect the arm’s lymph collectors to the veins.
expectation: The ducts will return collected lymph to the blood.

effect: The ducts completed the return route from the arm’s lymph collectors to the bloodstream, completing the goal.
reaction: The final inset brought the blood supply and fluid return together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the tissue spaces to lymphatic capillaries was most worthwhile: the described flap-like openings showed how fluid and proteins enter the return route.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lymph pathways to the arm felt less informative than the other steps; the result mainly showed where the collectors belonged.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the return ducts directly to the lymph pathways, but the pathways first had to be connected to the supplied arm.

arbitrary.text: That required order felt somewhat arbitrary because the duct picture already showed a connection to veins. The compatibility feedback resolved it automatically.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: seeing how the blood and lymph routes support the same working arm made me curious about how another body system would connect.
